Class ChaosAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.spring.boot.common.ChaosAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration @Conditional(OnTrustedChaosEnablementCondition.class) @EnableConfigurationProperties(ChaosProperties.class) @Import(ChaosSessionPropagationConfiguration.class) public class ChaosAutoConfiguration extends Object
Auto-configuration that wires the chaos agent runtime into a Spring Boot application. Shared between the Spring Boot 3 and Spring Boot 4 starters — this class only uses APIs that are stable across both versions.

Registration: META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports in each version-specific starter points at this class.

All beans are gated behind macstab.chaos.enabled=true from a trusted property source, decided by TrustedChaosEnablement — the same rule the early-attach EnvironmentPostProcessor applies. When disabled, no chaos infrastructure is loaded into the application context.

  • Method Details

    • chaosControlPlane

      @Bean(destroyMethod="") @ConditionalOnMissingBean public ChaosControlPlane chaosControlPlane()
      Exposes the installed ChaosControlPlane as a Spring-managed bean.

      The control plane is a JVM-wide singleton held by ChaosAgentBootstrap.RUNTIME; it outlives any single application context and is shared by every context in the JVM (common in test suites), and by a -javaagent startup plan. destroyMethod = "" is required: ChaosControlPlane is AutoCloseable, so Spring's default inferred destroy method would call close() on context shutdown and tear down every scenario, listener and the JFR sink JVM-wide. Per-context cleanup is handled by ChaosHandleRegistry, which stops only the handles it registered.

      Returns:
      the installed control plane

    • chaosStartupApplier

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean(name="chaosStartupApplier") public org.springframework.context.ApplicationListener<org.springframework.boot.context.event.ApplicationReadyEvent> chaosStartupApplier(ChaosControlPlane controlPlane, ChaosProperties properties, ChaosHandleRegistry handleRegistry, org.springframework.core.env.ConfigurableEnvironment environment, org.springframework.context.ApplicationContext applicationContext)
      Applies the optional startup plan file and the optional debug dump once the application context is fully started.

      The plan belongs to the context, not to the ChaosControlPlane bean: it is activated on the JVM-wide control plane (ChaosPlatform.installLocally()), so a test's tracking bean does not stop it when a test class ends, and it stops when the last context holding it closes (ChaosHandleRegistry.activateShared(ChaosControlPlane, ChaosPlan)). Only this context's own ready event applies it; a child context's event, which reaches its parents too, does not.

      Parameters:
      controlPlane - the chaos control plane bean, for the debug dump
      properties - the chaos configuration properties
      handleRegistry - the starter-local handle registry
      environment - the environment, to check where config-file comes from
      applicationContext - this context
      Returns:
      an ApplicationListener that performs the startup work
